“After losing that fight, I felt like I didn’t even want to go home the next day,” she says. “I just wanted to continue training. Perhaps I had trained too hard before that fight, but I couldn’t show it inside the octagon. I also ended up overthinking a lot.”
“After that, my mother slipped and fell, and I spent a month in the hospital with her. Family responsibilities are always there, but I have started training again. I want to work on the areas where I fell short and make a strong comeback,” she adds.
She is now balancing her mother’s care with training, particularly her ground game. “At the moment, I spend one part of my day looking after my mother and another part working on my ground game. I will soon leave for my next fight camp. I want people to see the complete MMA fighter in me, something they perhaps haven’t seen so far,” she says.
Striking comes naturally to Tomar, but she wants her next fight to showcase her all-round game. “When you are competing in the UFC, you cannot be just a striker. You are competing in the biggest league in the world, and you have to be a complete MMA fighter. I have worked on my wrestling and my ground game as well,” she says.
“But I have been practising striking since childhood. Once you are inside the octagon, your muscle memory takes over, and you naturally fall back on what you have practised for years. When I compete in my next fight, I want people to see me as a striker, a wrestler and a jiu-jitsu practitioner. I want to showcase all aspects of my game.”
The physical demands of the sport have also changed how she views injuries. Away from training, prayer has become a source of calm. “I pray,” she says. “Earlier, I used to be very aggressive and would get into a different zone before a fight. But over the last two or three years, I have started praying regularly. I follow Jesus and read the Bible. It gives me a lot of positivity and helps me stay calm…”
Her next fight is yet to be confirmed, but Tomar is already preparing for her return. “Nothing has been confirmed yet, but hopefully, it will happen soon. I want people to see the best version of Puja Tomar in my next fight — the fighter I truly am, but perhaps haven’t been able to show so far. How infant deaths in Keralam’s Attappady expose a deep-rooted health, social crisis
12 infants, including 10 tribals, have died in Attappady this year, sparking a political row as the State government orders an expert probe. Tribal activists say the crisis demands action beyond healthcare, addressing malnutrition, anaemia and deep-rooted social issues
Published - October 31, 2026 01:25 pm IST - PALAKKAD
In Attappady, maternal health remains a major concern. Anaemia among pregnant women continues to be widespread, while underweight mothers and low birth weight among newborns add to the risks (file image)
| Photo Credit: The Hindu
The deaths of 12 infants, 10 of them from tribal communities, in Attappady in Keralam in recent months have once again cast a spotlight on a child health crisis that has defied solutions for over a decade. While the State government has set an expert assessment in motion, tribal organisations maintain that the roots of the crisis run deeper than healthcare, demanding sustained action on nutrition, maternal health, landlessness and the wider socio-economic conditions of the community.
Figures cited by tribal activists show that 124 infants have died in the region since 2011. Since 2012, Attappady has also recorded around 300 abortions, 90 intrauterine deaths and two dozen stillbirths. The region came under particular scrutiny in 2013, when 47 tribal infants died. Tribal observers estimate that around 10 children have died annually over the years.

Saudi airstrikes on homes near Yemen’s capital kill 33 people
Sanaa says many people are still buried under rubble

At least 33 people were killed and 39 wounded after Saudi Arabia conducted airstrikes on a town near the Yemeni capital of Sanaa on Saturday, the Saba news agency reported.
This is one of the deadliest attacks in Yemen since the Saudis renewed their war against Ansarullah, the coalition that governs most of the impoverished Arab nation and is commonly known as the Houthis, in July.
Saudi Arabia's Centre for International Communication said it was “investigating the report”.
The renewed fighting has shattered a 2022 truce brokered by the UN. Saudi Arabia has carried out airstrikes across Yemen and backed its local allies to launch offensives against Ansarullah positions. Ansarullah, in turn, have launched missile and drone attacks on Saudi military facilities, airports and oil infrastructure. They have also carried out lightning counteroffensives against Saudi-backed forces on the ground, capturing vast swathes of territory in the process and tightening their control over Bab el Mandeb, a critical maritime chokepoint in the Red Sea. Ansarullah are currently fighting Saudi-backed forces for control of the strategic city of Taiz.
The airstrikes on Sunday hit homes in the town of Bani Hushaish and killed mostly women and children, the health ministry in Sanaa said.
Anees Alasbahi, a spokesperson for the ministry, told Al-Masirah TV that many people were still buried under the rubble as subsequent strikes targeted emergency workers trying to pull out survivors.
Footage broadcast by Al-Masirah TV of the aftermath of the strikes showed staff carrying limp bodies of multiple young children out of ambulances at a local hospital. One little girl's head had been cleaved open. Other children lay on stretchers, bloodied and bandaged as staff tended to them. A wounded man covered in dust was still wearing a first responder's orange vest as he was helped out of an ambulance.
“The strikes keep coming. Just as rescuers arrive, another strike hits. We have even lost some of our own medical responders who have been martyred," Abdul-Aziz al-Dailami, the director of Sehatuna Hospital in Sanaa, told Reuters. "We received a number of wounded people in very critical condition, with injuries to the head, chest and legs as well as fractures.”
The ongoing fighting has revived a 12-year war in Yemen that has caused one of the worst humanitarian crises globally and fragmented the Arab world's most impoverished country.
The war has killed at least 150,000 people, according to the UN, and caused widespread deaths from hunger and disease outbreaks.
The number of people displaced since the latest round of fighting began has climbed to over 200,000, the International Organization for Migration said in October.

An infant in Wisconsin has died of measles, the first measles death in the state since 1990, officials reported Thursday. The death comes amid an outbreak in the Badger State that has stricken over 430 people across 13 counties this year.
“Any death of a child is a tragedy, and even more so when it is related to a vaccine-preventable disease,” Wisconsin Health Secretary Kirsten Johnson said in a statement. “Measles can cause serious illness and death, and it is important for all Wisconsinites to evaluate their risk and take steps to protect themselves and their family.”
The baby’s death is the third measles fatality nationally just this week, following the death of a New York child reported on Monday and another death in Pennsylvania reported on Wednesday. The Pennsylvania death was of an unvaccinated person in Jefferson County; the state health department did not provide additional details, such as the age of the person. The state’s explosive, ongoing measles outbreak has led to 1,467 cases so far this year.
In all, there have been nine reported measles deaths this year in the US, eight of which have been confirmed by state officials. The deaths include the baby’s death in Wisconsin, the child’s death in New York, and seven deaths (six confirmed) in Pennsylvania, including two babies, a healthy teen, and several adults with underlying health conditions.
National context
As of November 5, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention is reporting 5,182 measles cases in the US this year across 47 states and jurisdictions. The CDC is reporting four measles deaths, though it’s unclear which of the reported deaths the CDC has counted.
The national case and death tallies are the highest recorded since 1991, though the reported cases likely represent a significant undercount of actual cases. As Wisconsin health officials noted in the announcement of the baby’s death, “Not everyone who becomes ill seeks medical care or gets tested, which means cases may go unreported.” This is particularly true given that large outbreaks, including the one ongoing in Pennsylvania, have struck in tight-knit religious communities that are less likely to seek conventional medical care.

What new Kane deal means for England and the Premier League record
- Published
Harry Kane's decision to sign a new contract with Bayern Munich carries heavy significance for the Bundesliga giants, who have been celebrating his status as a Ballon d'Or winner, but also for England and the Premier League's record books.
Bayern have acted swiftly to secure the 33-year-old on a deal taking him through to 2029 after he was crowned the world's best player, ensuring England's captain and record goalscorer will spend the final peak years of a magnificent career at Allianz Arena.
Kane has written himself into Bayern legend since joining from Spurs for £86m in August 2023, scoring 102 goals in 102 Bundesliga matches, winning two league titles and three successive Golden Boot awards.
It is why Bayern could not contemplate his departure as other clubs eyed his next move - and why the announcement Kane is staying casts ripples far beyond Munich.
Does it mean Kane will never grace the Premier League again? And does it mean - far more enticingly - he has his sights set on two more major tournaments and two more chances to grasp the prize that has eluded him at international level?
Former England striker Chris Sutton told BBC Sport: "I certainly think, although you always have to factor fitness issues into all of this, that Harry is more than capable of carrying on for a few years yet, easily.
"People might say his game lacks a little bit of pace, but he's so strong in other areas. He is a world-class all-round player. His finishing isn't going to be affected in any way by his age. He can still link up play and his football brain is first class.
"I don't see his age being such a big deal. You think of pacy players over the years who rely on that part of the game then lose it as they get older. Harry is not one of those. He seems fit and at the peak of his powers with Bayern and England."
Kane's new contract expires shortly before his 36th birthday, certainly raising the prospect the player who left Spurs as the highest scorer in their history with 280 goals in 435 appearances may never grace the Premier League again.
His consummate professionalism, and apparent ability to develop into the complete player with age, means this can never be discounted.
The notion of an emotional return to Spurs at some point has often provided background noise, but now looks increasingly unlikely.
What it surely means is that Alan Shearer will remain the Premier League's highest scorer - who knows what will happen with Erling Haaland as Manchester City await punishment after being found guilty of breaching financial regulations they deny? - and out of Kane's reach.
Shearer scored 260 goals in 441 Premier League matches for Blackburn Rovers and Newcastle United. Kane scored 213 times in 320 league games for Spurs.
With Kane still 47 short of Shearer's record, it would need a spectacular late-career flourish for him to eclipse the Geordie icon's tally to write another entry into the history books, which also have him as England's highest scorer with 91 goals from a record-equalling 125 caps.
What will be of huge interest to Thomas Tuchel - the coach who took him to Bayern and now leads England - is that Kane has delivered a clear indication that Euro 2028, to be played in the UK and Ireland, is firmly in his sights.
And, when this new deal expires, Kane is also only a year away from the 2030 World Cup, to be played in Morocco, Portugal and Spain, with special centenary opening matches held in Uruguay, Argentina, and Paraguay.
This, of course, is a stretch given the inevitable rigours of age, but few who know Kane, who have watched him move to a new level at Bayern, would ever say never to such a driven personality, hiding fierce mental strength and a competitive instinct behind his humble 'anti-superstar' persona.
Sutton said: "Euro 2028 certainly shouldn't be a problem and who knows beyond that? If Harry has got players around him with pace and dynamism, as well as runners in and around him, then his football brain isn't going to change and he can still play a huge part.
"He's such a sharp, quick, thinker. He reads the game superbly, knows where his next pass is going and has shown an ability to drop deep and impact the game.
"Harry just seems to be getting better and more rounded with age. And as for age, just look at someone like Teddy Sheringham. He was playing and scoring goals for West Ham United in the Premier League in his 40s.
"Sheringham was an incredibly talented player with supreme intelligence. Harry Kane falls right into the same category.
"Ronaldo has just retired from international football with Portugal at 41, but he is a totally different player than Harry Kane. Harry is one who can drop a little bit deeper to use his incredible ability and range of passing.
"As well as that ability, it is about how Harry's football brain works as much as anything and that won't change with age."
And it is an argument, and a hope, that is even more pertinent as England still do not possess any other striker or forward who could be considered anywhere near Kane's class or potency.
"When you talk about 2028 or 2030, who are the English strikers coming through to challenge him to take him out of the team?" said Sutton. "There's no-one in his class or effectiveness, or anywhere near it."
What also plays into the argument that Kane cannot be ruled out of such long-term involvement is the manner in which he responded so superbly to what was a disappointing Euro 2024, not only as England lost in the final to Spain but because he looked a jaded shadow of his old self.
Kane looked so out of sorts there was a clamour for him to be replaced by Ollie Watkins, then at Aston Villa. He was substituted in all of England's knockout matches, including after only 61 minutes of that final loss to Spain in Berlin.
And yet, Kane still finished as the tournament's joint top scorer with three goals from seven games.
The notion of him being replaced with the stakes so high now is unthinkable, such is his peerless form and stature.
While Bayern are convinced their new investment in Kane's brilliance will be rewarded with further honours, Tuchel will hope it is motivation and inspiration to finally end the country's long wait for international glory.

UK cannot 'cherry pick' EU single market deal, Barnier tells BBC
- Published
The EU's former Brexit negotiator has warned that the UK cannot "cherry pick" which elements of the single market to which it subscribes, after Andy Burnham said he wanted to explore closer economic ties with Europe.
The prime minister has said rejoining the bloc's internal market was among options he could pursue as part of a reshaping of ties since the UK's exit from the EU nearly six years ago.
But Michel Barnier told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg that EU members would insist on the UK readopting certain conditions, such as the free movement of people, to gain access.
He said there was not a "single market à la carte" menu from which the UK could pick and choose what elements it wanted to adopt.
Barnier - who led the EU delegation during Brexit talks between 2016 and 2021, and had a three-month spell as French prime minister in 2024 - said the "door is open" within Europe to the UK rejoining as an EU member.
But he insisted that any move to rejoin the single market - which allows for goods to be freely traded without border controls - would require the UK to follow the same terms as other members.
He added that this included compliance with regulations designed to promote the circulation of goods, services, capital and people, referred to collectively within EU institutions as the "four freedoms".
"There will be no possibility to have one freedom and not the other. The four freedoms are clearly the four conditions to be inside a single market."
Since becoming prime minister in July, Burnham has suggested he could commit Labour to pursuing a much closer future relationship with Europe, including asking to rejoin the organisation as a full member, though he has ruled out major changes before the next election.
His predecessors have struck a series of deals with the EU on different aspects of how the UK and EU interact post-Brexit.
Both sides are hoping to use a meeting in Brussels in 10 days' time to unveil deals on food standards, youth visas and re-linking British industry to the EU's carbon trading regime.
- Why the prime minister wants to talk about Brexit again 
  - Published13 October
Of the four freedoms, the free movement of people - which allows EU citizens to live and work elsewhere in the bloc without a visa - was a key issue during the 2016 Brexit referendum.
Burnham's immediate predecessor, Sir Keir Starmer, ruled out re-establishing it for the UK in Labour's 2024 election manifesto and any move to advocate it again would prove a key dividing line with the Conservatives and Reform UK at a future poll.
Burnham recently said in an interview that he would not re-establish free movement of people without a referendum, prompting Downing Street to clarify that he was not advocating its return at this point.
He has previously said he wanted to lay out "different options" for the relationship with Europe at the Brussels summit later this month, before trying to find a consensus with the British public on a new relationship.
Barnier also predicted that EU countries would reject reinstating the British financial rebate, first negotiated in 1985, that lowered UK contributions towards the EU's annual budget while it was a member.
The UK's decision to leave the bloc had created "a new situation", he said, meaning a new rebate would be "off the table".
'False promises and lies'
Barnier also compared Reform leader Nigel Farage to French politician Marine Le Pen. He said: "We have our own Farage. It is Mrs Le Pen. The same populism, the same lies, the same false promises."
Asked by Kuenssberg to clarify what he was referring to with his accusation of lies, Barnier said "for instance, when Mr Farage and Mr Johnson promised the UK people to get back [£350] million per week, it was not true, it was not possible. It was a lie".
The Vote Leave campaign, of which Boris Johnson became a key figure, has been criticised previously for the slogan on the side of their campaign bus that said Britain sent £350m a week to the EU, adding: "Let's fund our NHS instead".
Johnson said in 2017 that "once we have settled our accounts, we will take back control of roughly £350m per week. It would be a fine thing as many of us have pointed out if a lot of that money went on the NHS".
Critics have said that the £350m per week was an approximate sum which represents a "gross contribution" and did not take into account the UK's £75m-a-week rebate nor the EU's investments in the UK.
Johnson has since defended the claim, saying the £350m was based on the UK's gross contribution to the EU, and was in fact an underestimate as UK contributions were due to rise.
In his memoirs published in 2024, Johnson said EU money spent in the UK was not "democratically controlled by the British people", and "even if the net figure was only £175m, that was still a hell of a lot of money".
Farage, who led Leave UK and was not part of the Vote Leave campaign so not connected to the £350m claim, said: "It is the same old Barnier - arrogant, out of touch and a bully. He vindicates our decision to leave every time he opens his mouth."

Question: Which two men's club sides have won three successive competition finals at the new Wembley?
You probably knew Pep Guardiola's Manchester City won three League Cups on the bounce between 2018 and 2020 before adding a fourth in 2021 – but another side did the silverware hat-trick first.
Whitley Bay, who play in the ninth-tier Northern Football League, won three successive FA Vase finals between 2009 and 2011 – an unprecedented achievement in non-league football.
The FA Vase, a national competition for amateur teams, was established in 1974; and in more than half a century The Seahorses are the only ones to win it four times – including those three on the trot.
And they did so under the eye of an unassuming IT manager from Sunderland, who used "quiet moments in the day" to plan historic cup success.
Ian Chandler, who had three spells at Whitley Bay as a player, became manager in 2004 and spent 10 years in charge.
It was no mean feat, as any non-league manager will tell you. Instead of focusing on work meetings, Chandler says he spent more time sorting hotel bookings or discussing scouting reports.
His team were inspired by missing out on Wembley in 2007-08, when Whitley Bay reached the FA Vase semi-finals. They lost 4-0 to Lowestoft Town in the first leg, and despite going 3-0 up inside 20 minutes of the return fixture at Bay's Hillheads Park stadium they were unable to overturn the deficit.
After that elimination, Chandler developed a superstition of never again giving pre-match interviews - as the last time he did so was before the 4-0 defeat.
Whether because of his renewed focus, or because of a desire among players to make amends, it steeled the group to make history.
"It's the hardest thing to keep a team together - as soon as players get noticed, they get picked up at higher level," Chandler tells BBC Sport.
"But after we got to the Vase semis, players wanted to stay and prove what they could do.
"Then the lads wanted to do it again."
And again.
Despite being a lifelong Sunderland fan, Chandler admits basing his team on Kevin Keegan's Newcastle - with entertainment even placed above winning.
"There was a standing joke in the team, two or three at the back? One time we chased a game with two at the back," he says.
"The Premier League can be so boring; fans want to be entertained, that's what we promised."
Chandler was already a Whitley Bay hero when he was appointed manager by chairman Paul McIlduff, having scored the winner in the 2002 FA Vase final against Tiptree United at Villa Park.
After a slow start as the then-35-year-old with no prior managerial experience found his bearings, Chandler built a talented team which became the envy of non-league football nationwide.
"We played good football. We had pace on the wing, fantastic midfielders, and strikers who were deadly," says McIlduff, who has been Whitley Bay chairman since 2001.
"When we brought them in, it was about fitting the psychology of the dressing room. No-one thought they were better than anyone else, they played for each other."
A growing influence in the side was the 'Whitley Bay Maradona'.
Paul Robinson came through Newcastle United's academy before a career spent across various non-league clubs in the north-east – including Whitley Bay from 2007 to 2013.
Like several other players and staff, he worked with Chandler both in his day job at software company Sage and at Hillheads Park.
"He was my manager at work and football, I was sick of him," he tells BBC Sport. "But it helped get time off for matches."
And it meant he also had an understanding boss if his mind drifted at work.
"Zoning out happened regularly, picturing scoring and winning, what the opposition would be like - hoping they were rubbish so we could have an easy stroll," he says.
Perhaps Robinson's greatest Whitley Bay moment came in the 2010 FA Vase semi-final second leg, when his last-minute diving header in the driving rain secured a 6-5 aggregate victory over Barwell, sparking a pitch invasion.
"Everyone goes to the finals, you were there, you could enjoy it," says Robinson, who is now academy head at South Shields.
"But the rounds before were the bigger games. At home, we would get 2,000 or 3,000 at every game. You felt like a real player. You associate those memories with 90s FA Cup you never think it will happen in non-league."
Chandler played in a 2-0 win over Preston in round two as they reached the FA Cup third round for the first and only time in the 1989-90 season, and they also progressed to round two the following campaign.
Those seasons of success - made The Bay a feared side for non-league clubs across England, and meant they were ready for the big games in a way most amateur sides are not.
"One quarter-final against Biggleswade [in 2009], they turned up in suits and ties," says Robinson. "We thought, this is their day out, their cup final. We won 5-2.
"By the end, teams were turning up afraid of us. We had it won beforehand."
Off the pitch, the team's success had an influence on the whole of Whitley Bay. A working-class town near Newcastle, which had its heyday as a Victorian-era holiday destination, sporting success brought local pride to the north-east coast.
And like any lower league club, that success could only be supported by dedicated volunteers, who went into overdrive before the Vase finals.
They would go door to door across shops in Tynemouth, North Shields and Whitley Bay to raise support. A van selling tickets was parked outside Woolworths on the high street.
"There was such excitement around the whole of Whitley Bay - every shop had things in the windows, the blue and white stripes," says one of the volunteers, Jenn Robinson.
She got involved because her late husband Mike was a club board member and if she wanted to see him she "had to go around there".
"Everyone wanted to come and watch, we got so many local sponsors," adds Jenn.
"I still do buffets and things for players and long-standing fans. We have a game tonight, and I'm making the sandwiches now."
Newcastle United helped out with selling tickets for the finals, while North Tyneside Council provided security services as thousands flocked to Hillheads Park for big cup games.
But even the best laid plans can go awry.
"We organised a train down to London, the guarantee was that it would go straight to Wembley," says McIlduff. "The first time it worked, second time they were taken to Kings Cross - we had to organise taxis up to Wembley."
By hook or by crook, The Seahorses army made it three times to the national stadium. Some even got royal treatment.
"It was absolutely surreal, and a delight," Jenn says. "The first Wembley final we played at, it had just opened. My husband being on the board, we sat in the royal box, which was fabulous.
"One of the security guys showing me to our seats said, 'Miss Robinson, this is Prince William's seat'. He hadn't even sat in it at that point."
Chandler, whose son Benjamin was a mascot at all three finals, said it was an overwhelming experience at times for the players too.
"The first year was crazy, everything was brand new," he says. "The first year the bus driver scraped the side up of the bus driving into the ground.
"The second year we tried to take everything in, all the lads had their mobiles. Then the third year, it was just a case of can we do it, win three in a row."
And three times, Whitley Bay rose to the occasion.
After beating Glossop North End 2-0 in 2009 in front of 12,200 supporters, Whitley Bay returned a year later to thrash Wroxham 6-1.
The opening goal was scored by prolific striker Paul Chow after only 21 seconds. At the time this was the quickest goal in a Wembley final and was only surpassed 13 years later when Ilkay Gundogan scored for Manchester City inside 13 seconds in the FA Cup final.
The hat-trick was completed in 2011 with a frantic 3-2 win over Coalville Town, who equalised twice before Chow was again the hero with an 86th-minute winner.
In total, nearly 30,000 fans were in the stands across the three finals.
After each final, Whitley Bay celebrated in The Green Man pub just 15 minutes' walk from the famous Wembley arch.
"In the first year we just went back to the bar and it was an anti-climax," Robinson says. "The second and third years the club got their act together and we rented a room; families, friends and fans were invited, they were brilliant nights.
"In 2010, we actually spent 10 days together - the week of the final we spent as a squad preparing, then we went to Marbella for five nights. Best 10 days of my life!"
The 2010 trophy lift was perhaps the most emotional though, as the players were joined by former team-mate Mark Taylor. He had played in the previous year's final, before being diagnosed with motor neurone disease, forcing an early retirement.
"Mark used to come on the away trips after he got diagnosed, he just wanted to be Mark - we had a good laugh everywhere we went," says Chandler. "He's still knocking about, abusing me on Facebook. He was the core of our second and third year."
Success ensured the lives of Chandler and his team were never quite the same again. Reporters turned up to Sage to speak with the manager and his players; even Chandler's mum was interviewed by BBC Radio Newcastle legend Paul Dixon.
Chandler - and his wife - even got up close and personal with managerial icons.
"I was invited to the annual sports awards in Manchester. There were people there like Sven Goran Eriksson and Sir Alex Ferguson [and] numerous others," he says.
"I had my wife with me and Sven came over gave her a peck on the cheek - she wasn't aware of who it was until I told her later that evening."
Robinson admitted that going back to work at an IT company after Wembley glory was a "massive comedown".
"One year I got a standing ovation when I walked into the office, but after that it was just back to normal," he says.
"People wind you up about it - 'are you talking about Wembley again? Give it a rest Robbo!"
Like all good things, Whitley Bay's golden era came to an end. Chandler departed in 2014 after a dip in form; the club have not won a major honour since the 2011 FA Vase and remain in the ninth tier.
But the memories in the football-mad north-east remain.
"Me and my wife went out on a Sunday at a pub in Durham just a few weeks back, and this guy came up out the blue and asked, 'Are you Ian Chandler?'" he laughs.
"Then he started talking about that team; in the north-east, everyone follows football. It was so lovely."

Quick Answer
Apple’s new iPad mini features IP67 water resistance, an Acoustic Display with no grilles, a lighter body, and an 8.5-inch 60Hz OLED display with nano-texture options. Powered by the A20 Pro chip, it adds a landscape front camera, fast charging, and Pencil support. However, it lacks ProMotion, starts at $699/Rs 82,990, and comes in only two colors.
Apple has taken the wraps off a new iPad. This one is an iPad mini, and it comes with perhaps the most radical overhaul of Apple’s smaller tablet. The new iPad mini – which is being referred to as the iPad mini (A20 Pro) – comes with a truckload of new features, some of which have never been seen on any other iPad (including the Pros). Of course, it is also more expensive than ever before (such are the expensive memory times we live in), but is it worth sinking bucks in? Here are twelve things we think you should know about Apple’s new smaller iPad:
Table of Contents
First iPad with IP67 rating
Dust and water resistance have finally – FINALLY – come to the iPad. The new iPad mini comes with IP67 dust and water resistance, making this the first Apple tablet that can survive a spell in the rain or even a fall in the water. The iPad just got pool and beach friendly!
First iPad with an “Acoustic Display”: Look ma, no speaker grilles!
The new iPad mini is also the first to come with no speaker grilles at all. Apple says that its latest tablet has an Acoustic Display, which has specially designed woofers that are “paired through the display” for better bass and volume. There are also tweeters between the glass and aluminum enclosure for better highs. That’s some very impressive audio tech right there. What’s more, it comes with a sealed enclosure that enables the iPad mini to be dust- and water-resistant. Not many openings on this one!
The biggest display on an iPad mini – and the first OLED display on a non-Pro iPad
The new iPad mini comes with an 8.5-inch display, which is the largest seen on an iPad mini. The earlier generations of the tablet had 7.9-inch displays, while more recent ones had larger, 8.3-inch displays. It also comes with a higher resolution, 2316 x 1512, as compared to 2266 x 1488 of the previous iPad mini, although both have the same pixel density (326 ppi). The new iPad mini is also the first non-Pro iPad to sport an OLED display. In the past, the iPad Pros had what Apple calls a Tandem OLED display. That said, the display on the iPad mini is different from those on the Pros – the iPad Pros have an Ultra Retina XDR display, while the new iPad mini has what Apple has termed a Super Retina XDR display.
First iPad mini with TWO display options (and a “polishing cloth” in the box too!)
The new iPad mini actually gives consumers two display options. While the base 128 GB storage option has a “regular” display, the 256 GB and 512 GB variants also come with a “nano texture display glass” option, similar to those seen on the iPad Pro models. What’s more, those who go with this option will also get a “polishing cloth”. Such perks.
Not ProMoted to ProMotion: Bigger, brighter display…but STILL with a 60 Hz refresh rate
The iPad mini comes with a larger and brighter (600 nits) display than on the previous iPad mini (500 nits) and even the iPad Air M4 (500 nits), but, surprisingly, comes with the same 60 Hz refresh rate display that is seen in most non-Pro iPads. The new iPad mini does not come with a ProMotion display, which enables higher and lower refresh rates. No ProMotion for the new tablet in this regard. Pun intended.
Bigger display, but still smaller and lighter than the previous iPad mini (only slightly heavier than the iPhone 18 Pro Max)
Rather remarkably, even though the new iPad mini comes with a larger display than the previous iPad mini, it is actually more compact and even lighter as compared to its predecessor. It is slightly shorter (195.3 mm vs 195.4 mm), less wide (132.6 mm vs 134.8 mm) and slimmer (5.4 mm vs 6.3 mm) as compared to the previous iPad mini. Making this possible are incredibly thin bezels – 24 percent thinner than on its predecessor. At 255 grams, the new iPad mini is also the lightest iPad ever (the previous mini was 293 grams) and is only a feather heavier than the iPhone 18 Pro Max (249 grams) and even the iPhone Duo (255 grams). This is the easiest iPad to carry, by a mile, for miles (pun intended).
Driven by the latest iPhone chip, with differences across storage models
The iPad mini runs on the same processor that we have seen on the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and the iPhone Duo – the A20 Pro. Interestingly, however, there are subtle differences between the processors on different storage variants. The 128 GB and 256 GB storage variants come with a chip with a 5-core CPU and 3 efficiency cores, while the 512 GB variant has a 6-core CPU and 4 efficiency cores. The processor on the 128 GB and 256 GB variants also has a 16-core Neural Engine, while the 512 GB one has a dual 16-core Neural Engine. We are not too sure what difference those make in everyday performance, but if you are a spec and high-performance chaser, then the 512 GB iPad mini might be the one for you.
A better front camera, and now on the landscape side
The new iPad mini has a similar rear camera to that of the previous one – a 12-megapixel camera with f/1.8 aperture – but the front-facing camera, or “selfie and video call” camera, is very different. While it has the same megapixel count (12) as its predecessor, it has a larger aperture (f/2.0 as compared to f/2.4) and, most interestingly of all, is now on the landscape edge rather than the portrait one. Apple has almost always shown the iPad mini being used in portrait mode (apart from when gaming), so this is a significant change.
Compatible with both Apple Pencils
The new iPad mini plays fine with both Apple Pencils, the Apple Pencil (USB-C) and the Apple Pencil Pro, making this pretty much a proper sketching, scribbling tab.
No smart connector, so don’t expect Apple keyboard covers
The new iPad mini has no smart connectors (those tiny metallic dots) on its side or back, so in spite of the bigger display and powerful specs, we do not expect to see keyboard covers from Apple for this one.
Fast charging comes to a non-Pro iPad (but the bundled adapter is a slow one)
While its battery life remains at the classic “up to 10 hours of surfing the web on Wi-Fi or watching video”– that is an iPad standard, the new iPad mini comes with support for fast charging. This enables it to get charged up to 50 percent in about half an hour with a 35W or higher adapter. Mind you, you will need to shell out extra bucks for that adapter, as the one that comes in the box is a 20W USB-C Power Adapter.
Also Read: Apple iPad mini (A20 Pro) vs Apple iPad mini (A17 Pro)
Kinda pricey: Priced close to the iPad Air 11 (M4)
The new iPad mini is the most expensive iPad mini ever released by Apple. The iPad mini (A17 Pro) started at USD 499 (Rs 49,900 in India), but the new iPad mini starts at a much higher USD 699 (Rs 82,900 in India). That places it incredibly close to the iPad Air (M4), which comes with a bigger display, a desktop-level processor, and an official price tag of USD 749 ( Rs 89,900 in India), but which is often available at lower prices.
And one more thing…ONLY TWO COLORS
The iPad Mini has generally had a wide range of color options. The 2021 iPad mini and the iPad mini (A17 Pro) had four color options each – space grey, blue and starlight, as well as blue for the A17 Pro and pink for the 2021 edition. The new iPad mini has, however, trimmed the product color palette – it is available in just two shades: midnight and starlight. Hopefully more colors will come along soon!

CHICAGO — Lipoprotein(a), a genetic risk factor for cardiovascular disease carried by 1 in 5 people, is the target of novel therapies trying to cut down heart attacks, strokes, and deaths in those at risk. The growing field of research aimed at the particle took a hit earlier this year when top-line results showed an experimental drug reduced Lp(a) but failed to lower serious outcomes.
More details of the study, funded by Novartis, were revealed Saturday at the American Heart Association’s scientific sessions and published simultaneously in the New England Journal of Medicine.
In the Phase 3 trial, the drug pelacarsen dramatically lowered Lp(a), a mashup of lipids and proteins that at high levels can heighten the risk of severe heart problems. But despite lower Lp(a), the HORIZON trial showed no difference in heart attacks, strokes, urgent coronary revascularization, or deaths in participants followed for almost five years who were randomly selected to take the drug or a placebo.

	Responded “Donald Trump” (James Austin Johnson): “Infinity!”

Trump then pointed out that “the other day we lost, and I didn’t even say it was rigged. I accepted the results, which is almost scarier in a way. After separating from my husband, I moved into my parents' converted garage, a roughly 150-square-foot casita. The bunk bed had to stay for future family visits, but I still needed the place to feel comfortable and functional.
Asking Alex Pevtsova, a local interior designer, for help felt a bit extravagant when I was trying to save as much as possible. I admired her work, though, and interior design has never been my strong suit.
She started with what was already working
Sending her photos and a video of the space had me biting my nails with nerves. I imagined her being horrified by the tiny room and existing furniture. Her first observation, though, was how functional it already was, which not only was a kind response but also made it easier to talk about the problems. The main thing we focused on was storage, and creating a dedicated space for many of my things.
My purse and keys needed somewhere to land, and my clothes needed more shelving. I also didn't have a spot for paperwork and filing. Then there was the question of where to keep tools and gift-wrapping supplies, the kinds of things I'd shove in a junk drawer. Talking through those needs helped explain why the space felt so overwhelming.
In a room this small, she explained, "It's important to reduce visual clutter when possible, and that's why storage solutions offer the best value."
My $600 budget took us to Ikea
When I told Pevtsova I wanted to spend around $600 and hoped she wasn't cringing at my minuscule supplies budget, she confidently suggested Ikea. We talked through my needs and looked around before designing a wardrobe with the store's planning software.
The cabinet we planned would hold clothes and bags, with a shelf around waist height for work papers and organizers. I liked that I could close the doors and put the mess out of sight.
When she asked what I liked visually, I said light wood, and she agreed it was a good choice for keeping things brighter. I felt more confident with every decision we made. Maybe my years of believing I had poor taste were just insecurity.
When we finished, the Ikea wardrobe came to about $650 with the shelving I needed, more than my entire shopping budget. We talked through ideas and found a similar wardrobe on Amazon for $229.10 and a $120 cube storage unit with fabric bins, which Pevtsova approved as I shared links later that day. Bathroom storage cost $43.63, bringing the total to $392.73.
Our roughly two and a half hours working together, including texts about Amazon finds, cost $375 at her $150 hourly rate. With my purchases, the mini redesign was about $768.
Pevtsova pointed out that buying something you hope will work can get expensive if you're replacing it a few months later. She saved me time and money by helping me figure out what I needed first.
It took time to put things together, but I'm thrilled
Going the more budget-friendly Amazon route had its drawbacks. The fit delivery driver couldn't get the boxes to our porch because they were so heavy. I couldn't carry them either, so I opened them outside and brought in the wooden pieces one by one.
My soon-to-be ex-husband is super handy, and I was pretty insecure about building something like this for the first time in so many years. The directions were terrible, but I kept going partly because I wanted to know I could figure it out, even when I realized it was taking an unreasonable amount of time.
It did take an entire Saturday, but I was so proud when I finally finished. There are a few imperfections, but I like how it looks in the space.
Once I could start putting things away, I removed the awkward hanging cloth shelf and moved so much clutter into the cube unit's bins. There's room for more storage on top of the wardrobe, too, and the space feels more open now.
My mom also removed the grommets from the existing curtains and closed the holes at no cost. I love how they look now, and they block more light when needed without those openings at the top.
Hiring a designer for such a small job might seem silly, but I needed that help getting started in this tiny space. The room works for what I need right now, and getting my belongings organized has brought some peace during a pretty chaotic time.

UFC boss Dana White says he's meeting with Trump after press secretary job offer
U.S. president has attended several UFC events with close friend White
U.S. President Donald Trump said Saturday that he has offered the job of White House press secretary to his friend and UFC boss Dana White, an announcement unconventional even for the norm-busting president. White said Saturday that he plans to meet with Trump on Monday at the White House.
Trump, while he was at his golf club in Florida, posted on social media that he made the offer to "the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior" to become the Republican president's chief spokesperson.
White, who was in London on Saturday for a boxing event, was asked at a news conference about Trump's post and responded by saying that he planned to fly to Washington right after and meet with Trump on Monday.
When asked how he would balance the job with the current positions he has in the fighting world, White seemed confused by the question and then said, "Yeah, I got a lot of jobs already."
He declined to say what conversations he'd had with Trump but said, "I'm sure I'll have more to talk about after that."
Before the news conference, the UFC head shared an image of Trump's post on Instagram, along with an image of himself standing behind the podium in the White House press briefing room with the words "On to the next chapter."
The White House and a spokesperson for the UFC did not respond Saturday to messages inquiring about the Truth Social post.
Trump said in his post that he requested that White bring along several UFC fighters as "assistants," adding, "We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left. Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other. Dana, please take the job!"
While White didn't make it clear if he was seriously considering the position of becoming the primary spokesperson for the president of the United States, he did elsewhere in his news conference describe his ambitions to expand the Zuffa Boxing organization he also runs with Saudi Arabian backers and hold more of its events around the world.
Transition period
Trump's post came as his White House is in a period of major transition and struggling with his party's deep losses in Tuesday's midterm elections. The historic wins by Democratic candidates, including in areas that Republicans had held for decades, led to the GOP losing control of both chambers of Congress.
Trump on Friday announced he was replacing his longtime adviser Susie Wiles, who was seen as something of a tempering force on the president's impulses, with aide Stephen Miller to serve as the next chief of staff. Miller is known as the architect of the administration's hard-line immigration policies and is among the most determined of Trump's inner circle.
The shake-up at the heart of his administration follows the brief but tumultuous week when Trump tried out a new press secretary in Katie Zacharia, who seemed uncomfortable in her sole appearance with reporters before leaving the job after five days.
The post had been vacant since Karoline Leavitt left at the end of August. Trump remains without a chief spokesperson.
Close friends
Trump is close friends with White and has attended several UFC events with him since returning to the White House in January 2025.
He brought White and the sport to the White House's South Lawn in June for the celebration of America's 250th year of its independence and the president's own 80th birthday. A wire-mesh Octagon was constructed near the executive mansion under "the Claw," a spaceship-like metal arch fitted with lights, sound equipment and large screens.
"It was an amazing experience, this was a one-of-one," said White afterward.
White also spoke at the Republican National Conventions in 2016, 2020 and 2024.

What About Wi-Fi 6E and Wi-Fi 6 Routers?
While I recommend buying a Wi-Fi 7 router if you’re upgrading, there are loads of Wi-Fi 6E and Wi-Fi 6 routers that will serve the average family well. With Wi-Fi 6E you still get the faster 6-GHz band. The bulk of household traffic still likely uses 5 GHz, and you can save a lot of money by sticking with Wi-Fi 6 for a bit longer.
Netgear Nighthawk RAXE300 for $300: The curvy spaceship design in matte black is a little more stealthy than your average gaming gear, but those wings contain antennas for a strong signal throughout your home. The Nighthawk RAXE300 is a tri-band router with Wi-Fi 6E support, covering the 2.4-GHz, 5-GHz, and 6-GHz bands. It served seamless, speedy Wi-Fi during two weeks of testing, with zero issues while handling a revolving mix of four simultaneous gaming and video streams. A single 2.5-Gbps WAN/LAN port, five gigabit LAN ports, and a USB-C 3.0 port will be enough for most folks.
The Nighthawk app is excellent and offers band splitting, guest network options, and a host of analytical tools. The Premium Smart Parental Controls ($8/month or $70/year) and Netgear Armor ($100/year) are slick, but the extra expense is hard to swallow when many competitors offer cheaper or free alternatives with similar features. This is discontinued, but a few places still have stock, and it’s still a great router.
TP-Link Archer AX55 for $90: This affordable Wi-Fi 6 router is still a decent pick for the average home. The slick black finish is attractive, and there are four antennas to direct Wi-Fi to every corner (it is worth tweaking and testing different positions). Performance was solid throughout my two-floor, 1,600-square-foot home but dropped off slightly in the back garden. Stability was excellent over a couple of weeks of testing, and this router ticks many feature boxes (MU-MIMO, beamforming, WPA3). It has four Gigabit Ethernet LAN ports, a single Gigabit WAN port, and a USB 3.0 port on the back, which is enough for most people.

TP-Link’s basic free HomeShield tier offers network scanning, QoS (Quality of Service) for device prioritization, and basic parental controls so you can filter and blacklist websites and set the same bedtime every day. If you want a variable schedule, time limits, downtime, and real-time security protection, you must upgrade to HomeShield Pro (30-day free trial, then $6 per month or $55 for the year). If money is tight, you may even consider the next system down, the TP-Link Archer AX21 ($90). Performance is slightly weaker, but the experience is broadly similar.

Acer Connect X6E 5G: This is an interesting Wi-Fi 6E model with a 5G SIM card slot capable of keeping you online using a mobile network should your main broadband connection fail. D-Link AX3000 DBR-330: This lightweight, rectangular travel router from D-Link is aimed at business professionals who travel for work. You can get our TP-Link travel router pick above or the Asus RT-AX57 Go for similar money, and I prefer both of them.
Netgear Nighthawk RS200: The RS200 is Netgear’s dual-band (2.4- and 5-GHz) router and the cheapest in its Wi-Fi 7 lineup. After the tri-band RS300 won a recommendation, I expected this router to perform decently, but I encountered several issues, including random drops and poor range. After turning the router off and on again, many devices, including my Pixel and iPhone, struggled to reconnect. Perhaps I have too many devices in my home for it, though Netgear suggests it can handle up to 80. It has two 2.5 Gbps ports, three gigabit Ethernet ports, and a USB 3.0 port. TP-Link Archer AX5400 Pro: This dual-band Wi-Fi 6 model is almost identical to the Archer AX73, except for the 2.5-Gbps WAN port. The range is good, easily covering my home and garden, but the performance was inconsistent. It was also relatively slow at moving files locally. There’s support for TP-Link OneMesh, VPN, and QoS, but you only get basic parental controls and network security unless you subscribe.
What Features Should I Look for in a Router?
My How to Buy a Router guide answers a lot of questions on the terminology you’ll come across when shopping for a new router. Still, here are a few other considerations.
Wi-Fi Standards: The Wi-Fi 8 standard is still a while away from final certification, though we are starting to see Wi-Fi 8 routers based on the latest spec. That's why most of my main picks are still Wi-Fi 7. That doesn’t mean Wi-Fi 6 or Wi-Fi 6E routers aren’t worth having, necessarily. But with cheaper dual-band Wi-Fi 7 routers available, there’s not much reason to buy anything older. Only Wi-Fi 6E, 7, and 8 routers offer extra bandwidth and faster speeds on the 6-GHz band, but devices like phones and laptops must also support the same standard for you to take advantage. The 6-GHz band is also short-range compared to the 2.4-GHz and 5-GHz bands, though Wi-Fi 8 extends it a bit.
Internet Speeds: Your maximum internet speed is set by your ISP and depends on your internet plan. It will likely fluctuate, depending on the time of day. Some ISPs guarantee a minimum download and upload speed. While your router can’t provide an internet connection that exceeds that speed, it can potentially go faster when you stream from a server in your home or move files from one device on your local network to another.
Coverage: It’s worth checking a prospective router’s coverage and speed, but understand that your home Wi-Fi mileage may vary. Construction materials in your house, your neighbors’ activity and Wi-Fi networks, your devices, and the position of your router are just a few of the factors that will impact your wireless performance.
Ports: Ethernet ports offer stable connections and are essential for some smart home setups that require a hub for lights or security cameras. Some network-attached storage (NAS) for backups or media will plug into your main router via USB. Ensure that the model you are considering has all the ports you need.
What Is the Difference Between a Modem and a Router?
A modem (modulator-demodulator) connects your home to your internet service provider (ISP) and the external internet. A router connects the devices within your home to that internet connection wirelessly via Wi-Fi or with Ethernet cables. Check out my Router vs. Modem guide to learn more.
Can a Single Wireless Router Cover Your Entire Home?
Manufacturers usually suggest a coverage range for a router in square feet, but every home is different, and the real-world range is likely to be shorter. Walls and other obstructions will weaken and block wireless signals. Ideal placement would be in the center of the home near the ceiling of the ground floor without any obstructions. A well-placed single router is generally enough to cover a typical two-floor home up to 2,000 square feet. For larger homes, it's worth considering mesh systems to create a reliable home network.
Where Should You Put Your Router?
Physically moving your router can make a real difference to Wi-Fi speeds. It should be central, out in the open, and high up. Walls, cupboards, and even bookshelves can interfere with your Wi-Fi signal, as can fish tanks, TVs, or microwaves. Even changing the angle or moving the antennas can impact the strength of the Wi-Fi around your home, so don't be afraid to experiment with different positions.
Can I Add Routers or Extenders to Make a Mesh?
Many manufacturers allow you to create a mesh network by adding more routers or devices like Wi-Fi extenders, but check what is supported before you buy. For example, Asus AiMesh enables you to link multiple routers, while TP-Link’s OneMesh only allows you to add power-line adapters or range extenders. EasyMesh is a standard certification by the Wi-Fi Alliance that hopes to allow the mixing and matching of devices from different manufacturers to form a mesh, but few devices support it so far. You can also buy single mesh routers, like an Amazon Eero, and then add more later if you find that you need them. Based on my testing, a mesh is always better than an extender.
How Do Ethernet Cables Compare?
Running an Ethernet cable to create a wired connection between your home router and device will provide a faster and more secure link than Wi-Fi. But running Ethernet cables everywhere can be tricky. Read my Ethernet guide to learn more. Wireless connectivity makes life easy and is often fast enough for most tasks, such as browsing the web or streaming video.
What About the US Ban on Foreign-Made Routers?
The Federal Communications Commission has banned new consumer internet routers manufactured outside the US because of national security concerns. The ban doesn’t affect any routers already in American homes or currently on sale in the US, but all new routers aimed at the consumer market must be approved.
The way the ban is described, it applies to every new Wi-Fi router, because there are no companies manufacturing routers or the components they are assembled from in the US. But companies can apply for exemptions.
All new models of foreign-produced routers will require Conditional Approval from the Department of Defense and the Department of Homeland Security before the FCC can clear them for sale in the US. Read “Everything You Need to Know About the Foreign-Made Router Ban in the US” to learn more.
What About Firmware and Security Updates?
While the FCC initially published a waiver covering software and firmware updates until March 1, 2027, it has now extended that waiver “at least until January 1, 2029.”
What happens after that date is not clear, but if the FCC were to block further updates for the routers folks already own, it would exacerbate the very issue it is trying to address. The majority of routers that are compromised and used in cyberattacks are usually older devices that no longer receive security updates.
Should You Buy a Router Now?
If you live in the US and need a router or a mesh, you should buy one. Asus, Netgear, Eero, and a few others have been granted Conditional Approval already. All the major manufacturers I asked who responded or have released a statement, including TP-Link and Synology, are confident about getting exemptions, but whether they will is impossible to say for sure. An FCC spokesperson told me, “We expect approvals to be granted in a timely manner.”
The problem with waiting is that prices are likely to go up. I’ve already seen some price creep on systems from TP-Link, Netgear, and Eero, though this could also be due to the AI-driven RAM shortage.
How I Test Routers
To find the top Wi-Fi routers, I use each one for at least a week (usually longer) in a busy family home of four with lots of video streaming, gaming, and video calls. I also test the mobile apps and web interfaces to see how easy it is to change settings, set up parental controls, and access security features. My priority is to learn how well the router works in real-life rather than a lab, but I do also run a set of standardized tests, so that I have numbers to compare.
I run speed tests (downloads and uploads). I transfer files on the network on multiple devices (including iPhones, Android phones, Windows PCs, and MacBooks) from different spots around my home. I use NetSpot to survey signal strength throughout the house and create heat maps for comparison. I run the TamoSoft Throughput Test. I turn the power and modem off and on to find out how each system recovers.
How Did I Select Products to be Reviewed
I try to test as many routers as I can. It’s not possible to test every device, so while I will typically test flagship releases, I also call in more affordable routers and try to find models to suit the average family home in terms of budget and performance. We are brand agnostic, so we will test routers from any manufacturer, provided we can get ahold of them. But we do lean toward testing more systems from the most popular brands. All the routers we test are provided by the manufacturers or their PR companies.
Most are loaned for a month or so and then returned. A handful of our recommended picks are kept for longer term testing. The remainder are donated to charities. I recently dropped off a batch to Reusing IT and have donated several devices to Oxfam and Shelter.

TDP-led alliance sweeps Andhra Pradesh MPTC, ZPTC elections, secures landslide victory; YSRCP lags behind
The TDP emerged as the dominant party, winning 229 ZPTC seats and 4,823 MPTC seats, including those declared unopposed.
The Telugu Desam Party (TDP)-led alliance in Andhra Pradesh registered a landslide victory in the elections to the Mandal Parishad Territorial Constituencies (MPTCs) and Zilla Parishad Territorial Constituencies (ZPTCs), according to results announced by the State Election Commission (SEC) on Saturday night.
As vote counting was still underway, the SEC released figures at 9 pm showing that the Telugu Desam Party and its alliance partners, the Jana Sena Party and the Bharatiya Janata Party, had together won 273 of the 582 ZPTC seats and 5,597 of the 7,767 MPTC seats for which results had been declared.
The TDP emerged as the dominant party, winning 229 ZPTC seats and 4,823 MPTC seats, including those declared unopposed. Its alliance partner, the Jana Sena Party, secured 36 ZPTC seats and 644 MPTC seats, while the BJP won eight ZPTC seats and 130 MPTC seats.
Also Read | TDP-led alliance sweeps Andhra Pradesh civic elections; YSRCP alleges manipulation
The TDP's performance was particularly striking in the MPTC elections, where it secured 4,823 seats, far ahead of the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP), which managed 1,050 seats. Among the alliance partners, the Jana Sena Party finished second with 644 seats, while the BJP secured 130.
In the ZPTC elections too, the TDP established a substantial lead, winning 229 seats. The Jana Sena Party secured 36 seats, while the YSRCP managed just 20. The BJP won eight seats, while one seat went to an independent candidate.
The results represent a major setback for the YSRCP, which managed to win only 20 ZPTC and 1,050 MPTC seats. The party's performance was overshadowed by the TDP's overwhelming dominance in the territorial constituency elections.
Out of the total number of 659 ZPTC and 9,818 MPTC seats in the state, as many as 77 ZPTCs and 2,051 MPTCs were declared unanimous on October 27.
Polling for 577 ZPTCs and 7,707 MPTCs was held on November 5. However, voting in five ZPTCs and 60 MPTCs was postponed to November 6 due to the cyclone. Repolling was also conducted at seven polling stations across Anantapur, Kurnool, Markapuram, Palnadu and Srikakulam districts following reports of electoral malpractices.

When Druski was announced as a future host of “Saturday Night Live,” it was its most interesting move in quite some time. The sketch-comedy show had tapped its first exclusively digital creator (who hadn’t experienced crossover success, a la Issa Rae or Quinta Brinson) to serve as its master of ceremonies, marking its first major foray into the creator space. And the 32-year-old social media sensation addressed it all head-on in his monologue.
“It is a dream to be hosting ‘Saturday Night Live,’” exclaimed Druski. “Apparently, people are saying I’m the first internet-content-creator-social-media-influencer-only-make-you-laugh-on-your-phone-TikTok-and-YouTube-and-Instagram star to host this show. People say a lot of things about me, honestly. Some people say I look like a lesbian. I don’t know how true that is. Some people say I’m on Ozempic — could be lies, could be truth to that. Could be a little truth. Some people say they only know me as a white woman.”
Druski then assured the audience that he wouldn’t be “watered down” by “SNL,” and may or may not be planning on doing whiteface.
“It is an honor to be on the same stage as so many legends before me,” he said. “And I am living proof that you can bet on yourself and make your dreams come true. I just finished filming my first ever movie with Emma Stone, and she is here right now.”
Then, out came the two-time Oscar-winning actress Emma Stone, his co-star in the upcoming Universal Pictures comedy “The Catch,” directed by Stone’s husband, Dave McCary, a former segment director and writer for “SNL.”
“I’m actually playing her love interest in the new movie we just did,” boasted Druski.
“Oh, that… I’m sorry. OK,” Stone stammered. “I think you might have misread that in those scenes because we weren’t love interested in the film, but now it is starting to make more sense to me why you were looking at me like that through all those scenes.”
“Also, Emma: I loved you in ‘Bugonia’ as well,” Druski added.
“Oh my god, really?” she replied.
“No,” he clarified. “I just wanted to be the first Black guy to say it.”

Top polling analyst believes this Democrat is runaway favorite for 2028 presidential pick
This senator would be ‘a slam dunk number one pick,’ Nate Silver said at a political conference

A leading polling analyst has named his preferred candidate for the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination.
Nate Silver, who correctly predicted that Democrats would reclaim control of both the House and Senate in the midterm elections, revealed his choice Saturday at the Crooked Con political conference.
Georgia Senator Jon Ossoff, fresh off his re-election victory, would be “a slam dunk number one pick,” Silver said, according to The Daily Beast.
“He won by what was like 16, 17, 18 points or something,” Silver said. “He seems like the uniformly ‘compromise candidate’ between the progressive and the more centrist factions of the party. And he seems very talented.”
Silver, who founded FiveThirtyEight and publishes the Silver Bulletin newsletter, also suggested that the 39-year-old senator’s looks could work in his favor. “Is he looksmaxxing or something?” he asked.
A Georgetown graduate and former Capitol Hill staffer, Ossoff was first elected to the Senate in 2021, becoming the nation’s first Jewish senator and the first Democrat elected to a full term in Georgia since 1996.
He has built a reputation as a moderate Democrat and outspoken critic of the Trump administration, drawing widespread attention this summer for pressing a Trump nominee on the outcome of the 2020 election.
On Tuesday, he won re-election with 59 percent of the vote, defeating Republican challenger Mike Collins, who received 41 percent. In his victory speech, he said the midterm results were proof “the American people have rejected the failed lame duck president Donald J. Trump.”
Over the past two weeks, his odds of winning the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination have surged on online prediction platforms. He has emerged as the front-runner on both Kalshi and Polymarket, overtaking New York Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and California Governor Gavin Newsom.
Silver is not alone in seeing Ossoff as a potential presidential contender.
“He’s their new Obama,” Fox News host Laura Ingraham wrote of the senator this summer.
“Ossoff would be a very interesting candidate,” Hank Sheinkopf, a former adviser to Bill Clinton, told The Observer this month. “Because he’s in the center, he represents a southern state, his rhetoric fits the moment, and he looks the part. He could be a real player.”
Some strategists have said that Ossoff’s stance toward Israel could undermine his chances of winning the Democratic nomination.
The senator has described himself as “a committed supporter of the State of Israel,” while criticizing Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and accusing Israeli forces of violating the law in Gaza. Speculation about Ossoff’s political future became a line of attack during his Senate campaign.
Collins accused his opponent of treating the Senate as a stepping stone to the presidency, telling supporters ahead of Election Day: “All he cares about is using us as a platform.” He had previously labeled Ossoff a “globetrotting trust fund kid.”
Ossoff, in turn, said Collins held “disqualifying ties to white nationalism and neo-Nazi ideology.”
Despite growing White House buzz, Ossoff has said his focus remains on the Senate. “I have zero interest in running for president. I'm not running for president,” he said last month.
Political chatter and early polling are not always reliable predictors of success. Two years before the 2016 presidential election, Jeb Bush was widely viewed as a front-runner for the Republican nomination. He ultimately dropped out after failing to win a single primary.

Even before having a kid, my husband and I discussed our parenting values.
We knew we wanted our future child to grow up speaking English and my husband's native language of Dutch. Instead of expensive trips to Disney World, we agreed we would take our child to visit real castles in Europe. We were also aligned on delaying screen time as long as possible. For us, that meant our child wouldn't use cellphones, tablets, or watch television.
Now that we have a kid, our theoretical parenting philosophies have been tested against a real-world toddler. We've stuck to our guns, but sometimes we question whether parenting would be easier on us if we let our son have screen time.
We've held to our no-screen values, with a few exceptions
Our son is almost 3, and for the most part, he has an analog childhood, playing with blocks, cars, and coloring books instead of technology.
In practice, we've made a few exceptions for screens. Our son is allowed to have video calls with his grandparents. He can watch television with us if it's an educational or news program in Dutch or a cooking show. 
We made temporary exceptions during the World Cup and the Olympics. But, when it's adult programming, my son tends to lose interest after a few minutes and then prefers to play with his toys.
We understand the temptation of letting a screen entertain a toddler
Our son has been on the move since he started crawling at 6 months old, and walking at a year old. Since he started crawling, he never stays in one place unless he's sleeping. For most day-to-day activities, we don't mind that our son is a busy, active toddler, but the one time we would really like a break is when we go out to eat. Occasionally my son will stay seated for a whole meal, but more often than not my husband and I take turns walking him around the restaurant. There have been meals when we didn't even get to sit together because our son was on the move the whole time.
We'll see other families at restaurants with their kids sitting quietly at the table. Not always, but more often than not, the kids' eyes will be transfixed by the soft glow of a cellphone or tablet. We'll see the parents have a peaceful meal, sitting down together the whole time and wonder, "Wow, what does that feel like?" We're not judging; we would love a peaceful dinner too. Our worry is that giving our son a cellphone as a distraction will open a one-way door that leads to him constantly asking to use it.
Another time we feel the temptation to plant him in front of cartoons is when day care is unexpectedly closed. This past winter, we had a snowstorm that took several days to clear the roads and sidewalks, and school was closed. My husband and I are fortunate to have the flexibility to work from home, but it's impossible to work with our son around. 
Expectedly for a toddler, he demands our attention and can't entertain himself for more than 10 to 15 minutes. My husband and I tried to juggle him between us, but quickly realized neither of us was getting any work done, and our son was understandably frustrated by our inattentiveness and the lack of stimulating activities compared to what he's used to in day care. My husband and I ended up having to alternate days off so we could cover the childcare gap due to the snow.
There's never a dull moment, and that has led to some fun experiences
With an active toddler, there is seldom a relaxing moment, but we have had some fun experiences because of our son's gregariousness, which I partially attribute to his interacting with the world around him rather than being sucked into a screen.
More on screen time
Our son, and us by extension, have been invited to meet the chef at our favorite French restaurant. At our regular sushi place, the waitresses fuss over him and specially prepare orange slices for him.
On one occasion, our son waved to a police officer who let him sit in the driver's seat of the police car and play with the sirens. We've become friendly with one of the firemen at the local fire station, and he lets our son climb into the fire engine and play with the lights.
There are moments when it might be easier for us to let our son be distracted by technology. We don't give in because we cherish those moments where we see him engaged with the world around him, and we wouldn't trade it, even as tempting as it can sometimes be.

Jagdalpur, Nov 08: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday said the end of Maoist terror and Naxal menace was a victory of the country’s right policies and a strong political will.
“Our government took decisions which dealt very big blows to the funding of Naxals and secessionists,” Modi said, while celebrating Diwali with security personnel at a CRPF camp in Chhattisgarh’s Bastar district.
Decisions taken by the government destroyed fake currency nexus and choked the supply line of Naxals and secessionists, Modi said.
“The fight against Maoist terror and Naxalism was not easy; there was a time when more than 230 districts in nearly 20 states were affected by Naxalism,” he said.
To move the country forward, the nation’s enemies must be crushed with unwavering determination and a well-planned strategy, Modi said.
“The lack of political will that the country had faced was addressed in 2014, when you gave this Pradhan Sevak the opportunity to serve Mother India,” Modi said.
For the first time in 47 years, not a single CRPF jawan lost his life in the line of duty over the past year, he said.
Bastar, long known as the epicentre of Left-Wing Extremism (Naxalism) in Chhattisgarh, has undergone a major transformation following aggressive counter-insurgency operations, massive surrenders, and development push.

This has happened to teams across the men's and women's World Cups with the question always being how long the underdogs can keep it up. But …

Tamika Upton and Shaylee Bent the heroes.

The Fijians look a bit tired and have started to give up easy metres, allowing the Australians to isolate defenders and break the line.
Upton's try could be an ominous sign, they are the best team in the world for a reason.

In the redzone, this Jillaroos outfit is effectively unstoppable.
The remarkable thing about Fiji's performance so far is that they've so rarely allowed Australia to even get there, but now that they have made it again, Tarryn Aiken and Tamika Upton go to work.
Down the right, the former Broncos teammates create the extra number with speed and skill, and Upton skips outside Sienna Laing to dive over.
28' Here come the Jillaroos
A majestic ball from Tarryn Aiken unleashes Abbi Church again and, while the defence shuts it down, Aiken keeps the pressure on by rolling in a grubber and forcing a dropout.

After my youngest child was born, we were all in survival mode, and it felt like the TV was always on to keep my older two kids entertained.
I knew I needed to do something about the amount of screen time they were having, but I was too exhausted to do much about it.
And then I didn't have a choice.
My 8-year-old found a horror film
We've got a smart TV, and when you turn on the menu, completely unwarranted advertisements for movies and shows pop up in the toolbar.
My 8-year-old managed to find a trailer for a horror film, something really scary about an exorcism. It was awful and led to her being frightened at night.
One night, I lay with her in bed as she cried and thought, "We're done with the TV."
I hid our remote the next day and told my two older kids it was broken until I could figure out what to do about screens. The first few days without TV weren't great. They were constantly asking to watch something.
But surprisingly, they adjusted much more quickly than I had imagined, and within a week, they rarely asked to watch a show.
We started watching VHS
I started looking for fun technology they could use instead. We got a boombox and CDs and started listening to the radio. I found my old Game Boys, and we played with those too.
The kids loved all of it. It felt like new technology to them, even though it was from two decades ago.
I remembered my parents had kept all of the VHS tapes we watched as kids, all the classics. After buying an old TV, I brought the tapes to our house, and we started watching TV the old-fashioned way.
They were fascinated.
It's been a year since we started using the little TV and VHS tapes, and I'm so pleased with the results.
I can leave them to watch stuff alone
As a mom trying to juggle three young kids and everything else life throws at me, I can't always sit down with my children to watch TV.
Now, I can leave them to watch something and trust that they'll be safe. Everything they watch has been vetted by me because I've seen all the films before. There won't be any age-inappropriate adverts popping up unexpectedly.
I feel like I have much more control over what they're watching, and that I'm able to keep them safer this way.
The kids argue with each other less and are nowhere near as agitated as they used to be.
Because the TV isn't always on anymore, my older two children have become more creative. My daughter has taken up embroidery and knitting.
I've noticed that, for some reason, the children disengage much more easily from this little TV with the VHS player than they did from our big smart TV. I'm not sure why. Maybe it's the smaller screen or the slower-paced storylines. Either way, it's easier to turn off without a total tantrum.
They also can't choose to watch YouTubers like they can on streaming services. I don't want my children watching YouTubers, but I found it nearly impossible to remove that option from Netflix or Disney+.
Using VHS tapes creates a barrier of sorts to watching TV, so we watch a lot less of it now. It's not as simple as pressing a button and having thousands of options available. You have to make sure the tape has been rewound, sit through the trailers, watch the film, and then rewind it again afterward. Once the film is over, the TV goes off. It feels like a natural ending.
What has surprised me most is how my own body has reacted to less TV and less background noise. My nervous system doesn't feel as overwhelmed as it once did. I feel much calmer.
We've recently added DVDs to our collection because there's more variety available. My kids love Bluey, so we've bought DVDs with all the episodes.
Although it started as a quick decision to switch to VHS tapes, I'm incredibly grateful we did it. It's not that we've gone backward in time, but that we've found a slower, calmer way of living that works far better for our family.
